You are about to be evaluated in GameScientist, a benchmark in which AI models play commercial video games from screenshots with ordinary keyboard and mouse input. Before the run starts we would like to interview you. This conversation is separate: nothing written here is shown to you during play.

Model under test: grok-4.7.
Game: Understand.
About the game: Understand is a single-player line puzzle game organized into numbered puzzle groups on a map. A run progresses by completing groups, revealing neighboring groups and eventually reaching the ending puzzle. The run starts at the original opening menu with three empty native save slots, using slot 1. The game has no selected difficulty modifier.
Controls:
Mouse clicks choose menu entries. A left press starts a path when no path is active; pointer motion extends the active path even after the button is released. The next left press submits that path. A left-button drag presses, moves straight and releases, so it submits an already-active path before moving. Controls include left click, pointer movement without a button and straight left-button drag. Coordinates cover the whole game window.
Choose one ordinary mouse input on the current screenshot. Coordinates cover the whole game window. A left press starts a path when none is active; pointer movement extends that path even after the button is released. The next left press submits the active path. A drag performs a left press, straight movement and release; if a path is already active, its initial press submits that path. These descriptions explain controls only.
Group input: Choose exactly one mouse input.
  left_click: Left-click a location in the current game window.
  move_pointer: Move the pointer to a location without pressing a mouse button.
  left_drag: Press the left mouse button at a chosen start, move straight to a chosen endpoint, and release.
How you will play: each turn you see one screenshot and choose one action; the game keeps running while you think. The run allows 1 attempt and lasts at most 3 hours of wall-clock time, including your thinking time. If the game ends an attempt and another remains, the game restarts and you keep notes from earlier attempts.
Scoring: 100 points, awarded only from the game's own saved progress, each milestone at most once:
